assumptions: Within a bin the parts are interchangeable: each occupies the same slot in the assembly order.
For the end-homology chemistry, every adjacent pair already shares terminal homology, as the single-construct Gibson tool requires.
limits: Predicts the constructs, not their yields or relative abundance.
Combinatorial Golden Gate is served by the grammar-assembly panel, not here.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which constructs does this set of part bins make, member by member, and which combinations did a design rule forbid?

description: Design a combinatorial library in one step: SLOTS, each offering a bin of interchangeable parts, plus the CONSTANTS every member carries. The member set is the Cartesian product of the bins — one part per slot — pruned by design rules, and each surviving member is assembled by the SAME end-homology (Gibson/NEBuilder/In-Fusion) or plain-concatenation engine the single-construct tools use, so a member's construct is identical to assembling its parts on their own. It builds no second assembler; combinatorial Golden Gate lives in the grammar-assembly panel. Every pruned member is kept in the answer with the rule that removed it.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

bins.description: the variable slots: each {slot, parts} names a slot and the interchangeable parts (record names/ids, or wired `record` outputs) that may fill it. The member set is the Cartesian product across bins.

chemistry.description: `gibson` is terminal-homology assembly (Gibson/NEBuilder/In-Fusion/homology, one engine); `concat` is a deterministic head-to-tail join with no homology or digest. Values: gibson (End homology (Gibson)), concat (Concatenation).

constants.description: parts every member carries, assembled before the slot choices — the backbone and any fixed linker.

max_members.description: cap on Cartesian members enumerated, before pruning. Advanced.

min_homology_bp.description: Gibson only: shortest terminal homology that counts as a join. In bp. Advanced.

rules.description: j5/Eugene design rules that prune combinations: {kind:'notWith',a,b} (never together), {kind:'with',a,b} (if a then b), {kind:'notMoreThan',part,count} (at most count copies, constants included). Advanced.

topology.description: Gibson only: which products to enumerate per member. Values: circular (Circular), linear (Linear), both (Both). Advanced.

name: design_combinatorial_library

built.description: members that closed at least one construct

cartesian.description: Cartesian product size, before pruning (the product of the bin sizes)

members.description: every built member: its slot→part lineage, the parts assembled, the construct(s) and any flaws

pruned.description: every combination removed before assembly, each with the rule that removed it — never dropped silently

reading.description: what was enumerated, built and pruned, read off the run

record.description: the first member's construct, as a record
